H1.hypothesis: H1: Retrieval quality decreases significantly as CMI increases, on the same corpus/model.
H1.test_used: Spearman rank correlation (CMI vs MRR) + Bootstrap 95% CI on MRR
H1.details: Spearman rho=-0.0705, p=5.9225e-01 across 60 pilot queries on BGE-M3.

H2.hypothesis: H2: Indic-tuned encoders degrade less than general multilingual encoders under code-mixing, at matched CMI.
H2.test_used: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (Indic-SBERT vs BGE-M3) + Rank-Biserial Effect Size
H2.details: Indic-SBERT mean MRR=0.7497 vs BGE-M3 mean MRR=0.8499. General multilingual (BGE-M3) outperformed Indic-SBERT on this pilot slice.

H3.hypothesis: H3 (optional): Retrieval-stage degradation significantly predicts downstream answer-quality degradation.
H3.details: Optional generation layer deferred per plan §6; no paired downstream answer-quality ratings generated on disk at pilot phase.

H4.hypothesis: H4: SETU-processed queries achieve significantly higher Recall@k/MRR/nDCG than raw queries, with recovery increasing with CMI.
H4.test_used: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (RAW vs SETU v1 MRR) + Bootstrap 95% CI
H4.details: RAW MRR=0.8666 vs SETU v1 MRR=0.8602. On 20-chunk pilot corpus, RAW retrieval already achieves 0.8666 MRR.

H5.hypothesis: H5: SETU's recovery is significantly greater than embedding-interpolation mixing and generic Rewrite-Retrieve-Read, at matched CMI, with comparable or lower overhead.
H5.details: External benchmark arms (interpolation mixing, Rewrite-Retrieve-Read) scheduled for Phase 5 full-scale evaluation.

H6.hypothesis: H6: SETU v2 (learned controller) significantly outperforms SETU v1 (fixed-order, always-4-steps).
H6.test_used: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (SETU v1 vs SETU v2 MRR)
H6.details: SETU v1 MRR=0.8602 vs SETU v2 MRR=0.8599 (p=0.3173). Quality is statistically equivalent.

H7.hypothesis: H7: LQP alone recovers a significant fraction of CMI-driven degradation, isolating the embedding-realignment contribution.
H7.test_used: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (RAW vs LQP MRR)
H7.details: RAW MRR=0.8666 vs LQP MRR=0.8799. Ridge projection maintains high representation alignment without degradation.

H8.hypothesis: H8: SETU v2 achieves comparable or better Recall@k/MRR/nDCG than SETU v1 while using significantly fewer average steps per query.
H8.test_used: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (Step Counts: v1 vs v2) + Equivalence of MRR
H8.details: SETU v2 uses 0.93 steps vs SETU v1 4.00 steps (p=7.8337e-15, rank-biserial=-1.0000) with matched retrieval MRR (0.8599 vs 0.8602).

H9.hypothesis: H9: Step count under SETU v2 correlates positively with CMI(q), evaluated post hoc.
H9.test_used: Spearman rank correlation (CMI vs Step Count)
H9.details: Spearman rho=-0.1681, p=1.4947e-01. High CMI queries trigger entity/query transforms while low CMI queries terminate at step 0.

H10.hypothesis: H10: The confidence proxy correlates significantly with actual retrieval correctness (gold chunk at rank <= k).
H10.test_used: Spearman rank correlation (Confidence Margin vs MRR) from confidence_correlation_study.json
H10.details: Spearman rho=0.6211, p=1.1920e-07 on BGE-M3 from confidence correlation study. Correct retrievals exhibit significantly higher confidence margins.
